# Adjudication Task — Chapter 592

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃592화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|후우우.
  6|
  7|내뱉는 숨을 따라 붉은 안개가 피어오른다.
  8|
  9|그것은 숨을 쉬지 않는다고 착각할 만큼 길고 느린 호흡이었다. 아주 오래전, 스승으로부터 배운 비기(祕器)이기도 했다.
 10|
 11|
 12|
 13|‘항상 너를 지켜보고 있었다.’
 14|
 15|‘저, 저를요?’
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|벌써 삼십여 년에 가까운 세월이 흘렀지만 석고준은 그날을 잊지 못했다.
 20|
 21|부모를 잃고 친척들에게 버림받아 보육원을 떠돌던 그에게, 처음으로 꿈이 생긴 날이었기 때문이었다.
 22|
 23|
 24|
 25|‘너와 함께 지내는 아이들도 뛰어나지만. 너는 다르단다. 아주 특별하지.’
 26|
 27|
 28|
 29|대격변이 머물다 자리에 남은 것은 죽음과 평화뿐만이 아니다. 엄청난 숫자의 전쟁고아가 생겨났고 석고준도 그중 하나였다.
 30|
 31|많고 많은 전쟁고아 중 하나. 평범했던 그 역시 양계장에 갇힌 닭처럼 길러지다 사회로 방출되었을 것이다.
 32|
 33|그러나 스승, 이정룡을 만남으로써 그는 특별한 존재가 되었다.
 34|
 35|그것이 가장 큰 이유였다. 모두가 사라진 A구역에 홀로 남아 곧 들이닥칠 누군가를 기다리는 이유.
 36|
 37|스승님께서 머물던 이 공간에서, 스승님의 원수를 피해 도망칠 수는 없었다.
 38|
 39|“……진태경.”
 40|
 41|스산한 목소리와 함께 굳게 감겨 있던 석고준의 눈이 스르륵 열렸다.
 42|
 43|번쩍이는 붉은 안광(眼光)을 갈무리한 그가 본능적으로 자신의 목을 더듬었다.
 44|
 45|차륵.
 46|
 47|금속의 서늘한 감촉이 손가락에 닿는다.
 48|
 49|원래는 누구의 것이었는지 모를 이 싸구려 목걸이는 어느새 스승이 그에게 남긴 유품이자 가장 소중한 물건이 되어 있었다.
 50|
 51|모든 것이 잿더미로 화한 그 자리에 유일하게 형태를 보전했다는 이유 하나만으로.
 52|
 53|‘보고 계십니까. 스승님.’
 54|
 55|석고준은 주먹을 움켜쥐었다. 힘줄이 도드라진 피부 위로 붉은 기운이 아지랑이처럼 일렁였다.
 56|
 57|불과 두 달 전, 진태경에 의해 무참히 짓밟혔던 그였지만 이제는 상황이 달라졌다.
 58|
 59|석고준이 두려움을 이겨 낼 수 있었던 것은 그보다 큰 증오와 새롭게 얻은 힘 덕분이었다.
 60|
 61|‘놈을 죽이겠습니다. 바로 오늘, 이 손으로 직접.’
 62|
 63|착각일까. 아니면 우연일까. 목걸이에 박힌 검은 보석이 기이한 빛을 뿌리던 바로 그 순간이었다.
 64|
 65|구구구궁!
 66|
 67|공간을 뒤흔드는 거대한 울림.
 68|
 69|이것이 의미하는 바는 명백했다. 허락받지 못한 자는 존재조차 알아차릴 수 없는 이 공간이, 마침내 누군가의 침범을 허락한 것이다.
 70|
 71|만들어진 이래 단 한 번도 깨지지 않았던 수많은 마법과 결계가 지금 이 순간에도 허물어지고 있었다.
 72|
 73|“왔군.”
 74|
 75|조용히 뇌까린 석고준은 가부좌를 풀고 천천히 자리에서 일어났다. 최상급의 마법 방어구가 소유자의 뜻에 따라 전신을 휘감으며 솟구친다.
 76|
 77|촤르르륵!
 78|
 79|변화는 순식간에 시작되고 끝났다.
 80|
 81|검게 물든 전신 갑주를 착용한 석고준이 마침내 두 다리로 섰을 때, 모든 조명이 꺼진 복도의 끝에는 청백색의 불꽃이 도깨비불처럼 일렁이고 있었다.
 82|
 83|아니. 그것은 한 사람의 안광(眼光)이었다.
 84|
 85|“진태경……!”
 86|
 87|증오를 실어 내뱉은 세 글자. 그 이름이 주인은 석고준의 부름에 기꺼이 응답했다.
 88|
 89|“그래. 여기 있었네.”
 90|
 91|타오르는 안광과 달리 목소리는 서늘하다.
 92|
 93|하지만 석고준은 똑똑히 느낄 수 있었다. 그 안에 숨어 있는 불씨를. 오직 이 순간만을 기다리며 타오르지 않았던 심지를.
 94|
 95|그리고…….
 96|
 97|“고맙다.”
 98|
 99|화악.
100|
101|마침내 불꽃이 타올랐다. 용암처럼 들끓는 목소리가 어두운 복도를 달구었다.
102|
103|“지금까지 남아 있어 줘서.”
104|
105|미증유(未曾有)의 기운이 공간을 짓눌렀다.
106|
107|드드드득!
108|
109|더 이상의 기다림은 없었다.
110|
111|흔들리는 세상 속, 빛줄기로 화한 두 개의 신형은 복도를 가로질러 서로를 향해 쏘아졌다.
112|
113|푸르고 붉은 빛줄기가 맞닿은 순간.
114|
115|후우웅, 콰앙!
116|
117|눈부신 섬광과 하늘이 갈라지는 듯한 굉음이 터져 나와 사방을 물들였다.
118|
119|
120|
121|* * *
122|
123|
124|
125|적을 상대하는 것에 있어 가장 중요한 것은 평정심(平定心)이다. 이성이 흐릿해지면 마음이 흐트러지고, 마음이 흐트러지면 손발이 어지러워진다.
126|
127|그러니 평정심을 유지하는 것이 가장 확실하게 승리를 거머쥐는 방법이었다.
128|
129|이것은 현대와 무림, 어느 세계에서도 통용되는 절대적인 법칙이었고 나 역시 그렇게 해 왔다.
130|
131|하지만…….
132|
133|“진태경.”
134|
135|증오가 담긴 놈의 목소리를 듣는 순간. 어두컴컴한 복도 너머로 또렷하게 보이는 그 좆 같은 얼굴을 확인한 순간 나는 깨달았다.
136|
137|이성이 감당하지 못하는 분노 앞에서, 평정심은 아무런 방패막이도 되어 주지 못한다는 것을.
138|
139|한 번 타오른 불길을 걷잡을 수 없다는 것을.
140|
141|“고맙다.”
142|
143|눈가가 뜨겁게 달아오른다. 120층에 달하는 마천루(摩天樓)와 천여 명의 적들을 돌파하며 단 한 번도 흔들리지 않았던 마음이 격동한다.
144|
145|나는 눈 덮인 바위에 기대어 쓰러진 반백의 노집사를 떠올리며 말을 이었다.
146|
147|“……지금까지 남아 있어 줘서.”
148|
149|그건 한 방울의 거짓조차 스며 있지 않은 진심이었다. 지금의 나는 진심으로 석고준에게 감사하고 있었다.
150|
151|놈이 도망치지 않고 남아 있어 준 덕분에 내 손으로 직접 숨통을 끊을 수 있게 되었으니까.
152|
153|드드드득!
154|
155|끊임없이 공력을 소모한 단전은 반쯤 비어 있었으나 그것만으로도 충분했다. 나를 중심으로 퍼져 나간 거대한 파동이 A구역을 뒤흔들었다.
156|
157|지금 이 순간만큼은 계속된 전투로 누적된 피로도, 어느덧 무거워진 팔다리도 잊을 수 있었다.
158|
159|‘죽인다.’
160|
161|오직 그 일념 하나로 발걸음을 뗐다.
162|
163|염화일로(炎火一路). 지면을 박차고 나아가는 발끝에서 불꽃이 피어오른다. 복도를 점령한 어둠을 몰아내고 불을 밝힌다.
164|
165|그 끝에, 빛줄기가 되어 복도를 가로지르는 누군가의 신형이 있었다.
166|
167|‘석고준.’
168|
169|있는 힘껏 악문 잇새와 깊이 눌러쓴 투구 사이로 비치는 붉은 안광이 보인다.
170|
171|막힘 없이 쇄도한 놈의 허리춤에서 빛이 번쩍인 순간, 나는 백염의 창대를 곧추세웠다.
172|
173|후우웅, 콰앙!
174|
175|굉음 사이로 색이 다른 거대한 기운이 뒤섞였다.
176|
177|엄청난 반발력과 동시에 칼날이 되어 사방을 할퀴는 기파(氣波).
178|
179|맞대어진 무기 사이로 붉게 물든 놈의 안광이 보였다. 뒤이어 귓가를 파고드는 목소리도 함께.
180|
181|“생각보다 별거 아니군. 안 그래?”
182|
183|“……!”
184|
185|나도 모르게 눈이 크게 뜨였다. 마땅히 튕겨 나갔어야 할 놈의 두 발이 지면에 굳건히 틀어박혀 있었다.
186|
187|그리고 미처 예상치 못한 것은 그뿐만이 아니었다.
188|
189|까득. 까드드득.
190|
191|창대를 타고 전해지는 어마어마한 압력. 금방이라도 터져도 이상하지 않을 만큼 거대한 기운이 끊임없이 흘러나와 검신을 휘감고 있었다.
192|
193|천천히, 그러나 계속해서 크기를 부풀린 그것이 백염의 창대를 짓눌렀다.
194|
195|‘이게 무슨.’
196|
197|처음이다. 이토록 거대한 강기, 아니 오러 블레이드와 마주한 것은.
198|
199|눈을 크게 뜬 채 굳어 버린 내 모습에, 석고준의 눈동자가 환희로 젖어 들었다.
200|
201|“그 멍청한 머리를 굴려서 생각해 봤어야지. 내가 왜 남아 있었는지.”
202|
203|“너……!”
204|
205|내가 미처 말을 잇기도 전에, 놈의 검신을 휘감은 오러 블레이드가 폭발하듯 그 크기를 부풀렸다.
206|
207|카가가각, 꽈앙!
208|
209|귀가 먹먹해지는 굉음과 전신을 휩쓰는 강렬한 충격. 나는 눈 앞을 가리는 붉은 섬광과 함께 튕겨 나갔다.
210|
211|귓가를 스치는 맹렬한 바람을 충분히 느끼기도 전에, 단단한 대리석으로 이루어진 벽면이 등에 닿았다.
212|
213|콰지직!
214|
215|벽면을 겹겹이 둘러싼 방어 마법이 흩어지고 벽면 전체가 함몰된다. 서너 명이 들어가고도 남을 법한 크레이터를 남기며 벽면 정중앙에 처박힌 나는 눈을 깜빡였다.
216|
217|뇌에 가해진 충격으로 미세하게 흔들리는 시야 속, 이빨을 드러내며 쇄도하는 석고준이 보였다.
218|
219|“죽여 주마.”
220|
221|후우우웅!
222|
223|말보다 움직임이 빨랐다. 허공을 비스듬히 내리그은 검의 궤적을 따라 붉은 빛무리가 터져 나왔다.
224|
225|그리고 다음 순간, 수십 미터의 공간을 격하고 날아든 반월 형태의 오러 블레이드는 내 코앞에 들이닥쳐 있었다.
226|
227|서걱! 콰아아아아!
228|
229|그야말로 간발의 차였다.
230|
231|욱신거리는 몸을 본능적으로 움직여 공격을 피해 낸 나는, 오러 블레이드에 의해 난도질당한 공간을 바라보며 생각했다.
232|
233|‘만약 정면으로 막았다면?’
234|
235|정답을 찾는 것은 그리 어려운 일이 아니었다.
236|
237|지금의 나는 스스로 짐작하는 것 이상으로 지치고 피로한 상태였다.
238|
239|두 번의 몬스터 웨이브를 진압하는 과정에서 일섬의 여파를 고스란히 감당했고, 아레스 길드에 침입한 직후에는 대부분의 상대를 죽이지 않도록 힘까지 조절해 가며 싸워야 했다.
240|
241|이런 상황에서 저런 걸 정면에서 대응했다면…… 결코 좋은 결과를 볼 수 없었을 것이다.
242|
243|“진태경. 진태경. 진태경.”
244|
245|콧노래처럼 내 이름을 흥얼거린 석고준이 씩 웃으며 말을 이었따.
246|
247|“표정 한번 볼 만하군. 넌 영웅이 아니라 한낱 쥐새끼야. 살려 달라고 울며불며 빌다가 뒈지겠지.”
248|
249|나는 경쾌한 어조로 다가오는 놈을 물끄러미 바다보다가, 문득 뇌리를 스치는 어떤 생각에 불쑥 입을 열었다.
250|
251|“너, 약 빨았냐?”
252|
253|“뭐?”
254|
255|“아니지. 이 경우에는 약이 아니라 마정석이라고 해야 하나?”
256|
257|“……!”
258|
259|그 순간, 석고준의 입가에 떠오른 미소가 희미해졌다.
260|
261|이제는 굳이 대답을 듣지 않아도 알 수 있었다. 지금 놈이 짓고 있는 저 표정이 곧 정답이라는 뜻이니까.
262|
263|“허.”
264|
265|나는 작게 헛웃음을 흘렸다.
266|
267|잠깐이나마 정신과 몸을 마비시킨 분노가 옅어지자, 이제야 비로소 냉철한 현실을 바라볼 수 있었다.
268|
269|“그래. 그랬겠지.”
270|
271|괄목상대(刮目相對). 일취월장(日就月將)이라는 말은 한낱 사자성어에 불과하다.
272|
273|적어도 무(武)라는 한 글자 앞에서만큼은 그렇다.
274|
275|무력은 철저히 수련과 실전을 통해 단련시켜야 한다.
276|
277|시스템을 사용하는 나조차 저토록 가파른 속도로 강해질 수는 없는데, 하물며 그 대상이 석고준이라면 더더욱 그렇다.
278|
279|불과 두 달만에 사람이 이렇게 강해질수는 없는 법이니까.
280|
281|그러니 결국, 답은 처음부터 하나밖에 없었다.
282|
283|“빨았네. 빨았어. 이 병신 새끼.”
284|

[P69]
*Rrrrmmble!*

[P70]
My dantian was half empty after all the internal energy I had spent, but what remained was enough. A massive wave spread out from me and shook Area A.

[P71]
For this moment, I could forget the fatigue of the endless battles and the growing weight of my limbs.

[P72]
*I’ll kill him.*

[P73]
With that one thought, I stepped forward.

[P74]
*Flamefire Path.*

[P75]
Flames rose from my feet as I kicked off the ground. They drove back the darkness filling the corridor and lit my way.

[P76]
At the far end, a figure streaked toward me like a beam of light.

[P77]
*Go Jun.*

[P78]
I could see the red glow of his eyes between his clenched teeth and the helmet pulled low over his face.

[P79]
Light flashed at his waist as he charged straight at me. I raised White Flame’s shaft.

[P80]
*Whoom, KABOOM!*

[P81]
Two enormous energies of different colors tangled amid the roar.

[P82]
The collision sent a tremendous force back through my weapon. A wave of energy slashed in every direction like a blade.

[P83]
Beyond our locked weapons, I saw his red eyes. Then his voice reached me.

[P84]
“You’re not much, are you?”

[P85]
“…!”

[P86]
My eyes widened despite myself.

[P87]
His feet should have been knocked backward. Instead, they were planted firmly in the ground.

[P88]
And that was not the only thing I had failed to anticipate.

[P89]
*Crunch. Crrrunch.*

[P90]
Unbelievable pressure traveled up White Flame’s shaft. Power great enough to seem on the verge of bursting poured out and wrapped around his sword blade.

[P91]
It swelled slowly, steadily, bearing down on the spear shaft.

[P92]
*What is this?*

[P93]
I had never faced Force this immense—or rather, an Aura Blade of this magnitude.

[P94]
At the sight of me frozen there, Go Jun’s eyes filled with delight.

[P95]
“You should’ve put that stupid head of yours to work and wondered why I stayed.”

[P96]
“You…!”

[P97]
Before I could finish, the Aura Blade surrounding his sword swelled outward as if it had exploded.

[P98]
*Craaaack, KABOOM!*

[P99]
A roar left my ears ringing. A powerful shock swept through my body, and a red flash filled my vision as I flew backward.

[P100]
Before I could fully feel the wind rushing past my ears, my back struck a solid marble wall.

[P101]
*KRAK!*

[P102]
The layers of defensive Magic surrounding it scattered, and the whole wall caved in.

[P103]
I was embedded in its center, in a crater big enough to hold three or four people. I blinked.

[P104]
My vision trembled from the impact to my head. Through it, I saw Go Jun charging at me with his teeth bared.

[P105]
“I’ll kill you.”

[P106]
*Whoooooosh!*

[P107]
He moved faster than he spoke. His sword cut diagonally down through the air, sending out a burst of red light.

[P108]
An instant later, the crescent-shaped Aura Blade had crossed dozens of meters and reached my face.

[P109]
*Slice! KRAAAAAASH!*

[P110]
I escaped by a hair.

[P111]
My aching body moved on instinct, carrying me clear of the attack. Looking at the space the Aura Blade had shredded, I thought:

[P112]
*What if I’d tried to block that head-on?*

[P113]
The answer was easy enough.

[P114]
I was more exhausted than I had realized.

[P115]
Suppressing two Monster Waves had made me bear the full aftermath of One Annihilation. Then, from the moment I entered Ares Guild, I had fought while holding back enough to avoid killing most of my opponents.

[P116]
Facing an attack like that head-on in my current condition would not have ended well.

[P117]
“Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung.”

[P118]
Go Jun hummed my name like a tune, then grinned.

[P119]
“You should see your face. You’re no hero. You’re just a rat. You’ll die crying and begging for your life.”

[P120]
I watched him approach, his voice almost cheerful. Then a thought struck me.

[P121]
“Did you take something?”

[P122]
“What?”

[P123]
“No, wait. In this case, should I say a Magic Gem instead of drugs?”

[P124]
“…!”

[P125]
The smile on Go Jun’s lips faded.

[P126]
I no longer needed an answer. His face had given me one.

[P127]
“Hah.”

[P128]
I let out a hollow laugh.

[P129]
The rage that had briefly paralyzed my mind and body ebbed, and I could finally see the situation clearly.

[P130]
“Of course. That’s how you did it.”

[P131]
“Seeing someone in a new light” and “improving by leaps and bounds” were just four-character idioms. At least when it came to martial arts.

[P132]
Martial strength had to be honed through training and real combat.

[P133]
Even with the System, I could not have grown stronger at that rate. Go Jun certainly could not have done it.

[P134]
No one became this strong in only two months.

[P135]
There had only ever been one answer.

[P136]
“You took one. You really did, you fucking idiot.”

[P137]
I couldn’t hold back my laughter.

[P138]
It wasn’t amusement. It was disgust. Go Jun had chosen to give up being human and become a monster, and the sheer stupidity of it kept making me laugh.

[P139]
“Fuck, I’ve never seen an idiot like you. You couldn’t beat me any normal way, so you started sucking down Magic Gems? If you were going to do that, why not go to Magic Johnson? I bet that guy would’ve taken real good care of you with his magic wand.”

[P140]
I had hit a nerve. Go Jun’s face went rigid, and his already-red eyes darkened further.

[P141]
“Shut your fucking—”

[P142]
“Just shut up and listen, you son of a bitch.”

[P143]
*Thud. Thud.*

[P144]
Rubble and chunks of marble fell away as I got up.

[P145]
I cracked my stiff neck from side to side and stared at him.

[P146]
“What? You set off a few Monster Waves with an S-grade Magic Gem and pissed yourself over how well it worked? Watched people die because you barely lifted a finger and thought you were a god? No, sir, you fucking moron. You’re just a monster. At best, you’re some idiot side character with a Named Monster for a constellation.”

[P147]
“Shut up!”

[P148]
“Fuck off. Want me to give it a title, too? *Go Jun Swallows an S-Grade Magic Gem.*”

[P149]
“Jin Taekyuuung—!”

[P150]
*Fwoooooosh!*

[P151]
A gale rose with a tremendous wave of energy and swept through the area.

[P152]
I watched his power swell as if it were about to burst and answered calmly.

[P153]
“What, you fucking idiot?”

[P154]
I had never been afraid. Now that I knew what he had become, I had no reason to hesitate.

[P155]
He was a monster who had crossed the line, and he had to die by my hand today.

[P156]
For the old butler who had fallen into a darkness from which he would never return. For the people and Hunters who had died in the Monster Waves.

[P157]
And… for me, furious at this goddamned reality.

[P158]
“You have to die.”

[P159]
I bit out the words with all my heart. Go Jun’s blood-red figure blurred.

[P160]
*Whoooooosh! KABOOM!*

[P161]
The red Aura Blade stopped above my head.

[P162]
The tremendous pressure coming through White Flame’s spear blade made my wrists throb, and my ankles sank deep into the ground.

[P163]
But I did not give way. At least the power I wielded had been built through countless hours of training and insight, with the good fortune of the System added on top.

[P164]
“Get lost, you drugged-up bastard.”

[P165]
*Rrrrmmble!*

[P166]
I grinned into Go Jun’s wide eyes and drove my fist forward with all my strength.

[P167]
*Wham!*

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

[P38]
He spat the three syllables with hatred. The man whose name he had called answered willingly.

[P39]
“Yeah. So you were here.”

[P40]
Unlike the burning glow in his eyes, his voice was cold.

[P41]
But Go Jun could hear the ember hidden within it. The wick that had waited for this moment without catching fire.

[P42]
And then—

[P43]
“Thanks.”

[P44]
*Fwoosh.*

[P45]
At last, the flame caught. A voice boiling like lava heated the dark corridor.

[P46]
“For staying here all this time.”

[P47]
An overwhelming energy pressed down on the space.

[P48]
*Rrrrmmble!*

[P49]
There would be no more waiting.

[P50]
As the world shook, two figures became streaks of light and shot across the corridor toward each other.

[P51]
The instant the blue and red streaks met—

[P52]
*Whoom, KABOOM!*

[P53]
A blinding flash and a roar that seemed to split the sky burst out, filling the space around them.

[P54]
* * *

[P55]
The most important thing when facing an enemy was composure. When reason grew clouded, the mind became unsettled. When the mind became unsettled, the hands and feet lost their coordination.

[P56]
Maintaining composure was the surest way to win.

[P57]
That rule held true in both the modern world and Murim, and I had always followed it.

[P58]
But…

[P59]
“Jin Taekyung.”

[P60]
The moment I heard the hatred in his voice, the moment I saw that fucking face beyond the dark corridor, I realized something.

[P61]
Composure was no shield against anger reason could not contain.

[P62]
Once that fire caught, there was no controlling it.

[P63]
“Thanks.”

[P64]
My eyes grew hot. I had fought my way through a 120-story skyscraper and around a thousand enemies without wavering once, but now my heart churned.

[P65]
I thought of the silver-haired old butler collapsed against a snow-covered rock and continued.

[P66]
“…For staying here all this time.”

[P67]
I meant every word. I was sincerely grateful to Go Jun.

[P68]
Because he had stayed instead of running, I could end his life with my own hands.

[P69]
*Rrrrmmble!*

[P70]
My dantian was half empty after all the internal energy I had spent, but what remained was enough. A massive wave spread out from me and shook Area A.

[P71]
For this moment, I could forget the fatigue of the endless battles and the growing weight of my limbs.

[P72]
*I’ll kill him.*

[P73]
With that one thought, I stepped forward.

[P74]
*Flamefire Path.*

[P75]
Flames rose from my feet as I kicked off the ground. They drove back the darkness filling the corridor and lit my way.

[P76]
At the far end, a figure streaked toward me like a beam of light.

[P77]
*Go Jun.*

[P78]
I could see the red glow of his eyes between his clenched teeth and the helmet pulled low over his face.

[P79]
Light flashed at his waist as he charged straight at me. I raised White Flame’s shaft.

[P80]
*Whoom, KABOOM!*

[P81]
Two enormous energies of different colors tangled amid the roar.

[P82]
The collision sent a tremendous force back through my weapon. A wave of energy slashed in every direction like a blade.

[P83]
Beyond our locked weapons, I saw his red eyes. Then his voice reached me.

[P84]
“You’re not much, are you?”

[P85]
“…!”

[P86]
My eyes widened despite myself.

[P87]
His feet should have been knocked backward. Instead, they were planted firmly in the ground.

[P88]
And that was not the only thing I had failed to anticipate.

[P89]
*Crunch. Crrrunch.*

[P90]
Unbelievable pressure traveled up White Flame’s shaft. Power great enough to seem on the verge of bursting poured out and wrapped around his sword blade.

[P91]
It swelled slowly, steadily, bearing down on the spear shaft.

[P92]
*What is this?*

[P93]
I had never faced Force this immense—or rather, an Aura Blade of this magnitude.

[P94]
At the sight of me frozen there, Go Jun’s eyes filled with delight.

[P95]
“You should’ve put that stupid head of yours to work and wondered why I stayed.”

[P96]
“You…!”

[P97]
Before I could finish, the Aura Blade surrounding his sword swelled outward as if it had exploded.

[P98]
*Craaaack, KABOOM!*

[P99]
A roar left my ears ringing. A powerful shock swept through my body, and a red flash filled my vision as I flew backward.

[P100]
Before I could fully feel the wind rushing past my ears, my back struck a solid marble wall.

[P101]
*KRAK!*

[P102]
The layers of defensive Magic surrounding it scattered, and the whole wall caved in.

[P103]
I was embedded in its center, in a crater big enough to hold three or four people. I blinked.

[P104]
My vision trembled from the impact to my head. Through it, I saw Go Jun charging at me with his teeth bared.

[P105]
“I’ll kill you.”

[P106]
*Whoooooosh!*

[P107]
He moved faster than he spoke. His sword cut diagonally down through the air, sending out a burst of red light.

[P108]
An instant later, the crescent-shaped Aura Blade had crossed dozens of meters and reached my face.

[P109]
*Slice! KRAAAAAASH!*

[P110]
I escaped by a hair.

[P111]
My aching body moved on instinct, carrying me clear of the attack. Looking at the space the Aura Blade had shredded, I thought:

[P112]
*What if I’d tried to block that head-on?*

[P113]
The answer was easy enough.

[P114]
I was more exhausted than I had realized.

[P115]
Suppressing two Monster Waves had made me bear the full aftermath of One Annihilation. Then, from the moment I entered Ares Guild, I had fought while holding back enough to avoid killing most of my opponents.

[P116]
Facing an attack like that head-on in my current condition would not have ended well.

[P117]
“Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung.”

[P118]
Go Jun hummed my name like a tune, then grinned.

[P119]
“You should see your face. You’re no hero. You’re just a rat. You’ll die crying and begging for your life.”

[P120]
I watched him approach, his voice almost cheerful. Then a thought struck me.

[P121]
“Did you take something?”

[P122]
“What?”

[P123]
“No, wait. In this case, should I say a Magic Gem instead of drugs?”

[P124]
“…!”

[P125]
The smile on Go Jun’s lips faded.

[P126]
I no longer needed an answer. His face had given me one.

[P127]
“Hah.”

[P128]
I let out a hollow laugh.

[P129]
The rage that had briefly paralyzed my mind and body ebbed, and I could finally see the situation clearly.

[P130]
“Of course. That’s how you did it.”

[P131]
“Seeing someone in a new light” and “improving by leaps and bounds” were just four-character idioms. At least when it came to martial arts.

[P132]
Martial strength had to be honed through training and real combat.

[P133]
Even with the System, I could not have grown stronger at that rate. Go Jun certainly could not have done it.

[P134]
No one became this strong in only two months.

[P135]
There had only ever been one answer.

[P136]
“You took one. You really did, you fucking idiot.”

[P137]
I couldn’t hold back my laughter.

[P138]
It wasn’t amusement. It was disgust. Go Jun had chosen to give up being human and become a monster, and the sheer stupidity of it kept making me laugh.

[P139]
“Fuck, I’ve never seen an idiot like you. You couldn’t beat me any normal way, so you started sucking down Magic Gems? If you were going to do that, why not go to Magic Johnson? I bet that guy would’ve taken real good care of you with his magic wand.”

[P140]
I had hit a nerve. Go Jun’s face went rigid, and his already-red eyes darkened further.

[P141]
“Shut your fucking—”

[P142]
“Just shut up and listen, you son of a bitch.”

[P143]
*Thud. Thud.*

[P144]
Rubble and chunks of marble fell away as I got up.

[P145]
I cracked my stiff neck from side to side and stared at him.

[P146]
“What? You set off a few Monster Waves with an S-grade Magic Gem and pissed yourself over how well it worked? Watched people die because you barely lifted a finger and thought you were a god? No, sir, you fucking moron. You’re just a monster. At best, you’re some idiot side character with a Named Monster for a constellation.”

[P147]
“Shut up!”

[P148]
“Fuck off. Want me to give it a title, too? *Go Jun Swallows an S-Grade Magic Gem.*”

[P149]
“Jin Taekyuuung—!”

[P150]
*Fwoooooosh!*

[P151]
A gale rose with a tremendous wave of energy and swept through the area.

[P152]
I watched his power swell as if it were about to burst and answered calmly.

[P153]
“What, you fucking idiot?”

[P154]
I had never been afraid. Now that I knew what he had become, I had no reason to hesitate.

[P155]
He was a monster who had crossed the line, and he had to die by my hand today.

[P156]
For the old butler who had fallen into a darkness from which he would never return. For the people and Hunters who had died in the Monster Waves.

[P157]
And… for me, furious at this goddamned reality.

[P158]
“You have to die.”

[P159]
I bit out the words with all my heart. Go Jun’s blood-red figure blurred.

[P160]
*Whoooooosh! KABOOM!*

[P161]
The red Aura Blade stopped above my head.

[P162]
The tremendous pressure coming through White Flame’s spear blade made my wrists throb, and my ankles sank deep into the ground.

[P163]
But I did not give way. At least the power I wielded had been built through countless hours of training and insight, with the good fortune of the System added on top.

[P164]
“Get lost, you drugged-up bastard.”

[P165]
*Rrrrmmble!*

[P166]
I grinned into Go Jun’s wide eyes and drove my fist forward with all my strength.

[P167]
*Wham!*

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Before I could finish, the Aura Blade surrounding his sword swelled outward as if it had exploded.

[P98]
*Craaaack, KABOOM!*

[P99]
A roar left my ears ringing. A powerful shock swept through my body, and a red flash filled my vision as I flew backward.

[P100]
Before I could fully feel the wind rushing past my ears, my back struck a solid marble wall.

[P101]
*KRAK!*

[P102]
The layers of defensive Magic surrounding it scattered, and the whole wall caved in.

[P103]
I was embedded in its center, in a crater big enough to hold three or four people. I blinked.

[P104]
My vision trembled from the impact to my head. Through it, I saw Go Jun charging at me with his teeth bared.

[P105]
“I’ll kill you.”

[P106]
*Whoooooosh!*

[P107]
He moved faster than he spoke. His sword cut diagonally down through the air, sending out a burst of red light.

[P108]
An instant later, the crescent-shaped Aura Blade had crossed dozens of meters and reached my face.

[P109]
*Slice! KRAAAAAASH!*

[P110]
I escaped by a hair.

[P111]
My aching body moved on instinct, carrying me clear of the attack. Looking at the space the Aura Blade had shredded, I thought:

[P112]
*What if I’d tried to block that head-on?*

[P113]
The answer was easy enough.

[P114]
I was more exhausted than I had realized.

[P115]
Suppressing two Monster Waves had made me bear the full aftermath of One Annihilation. Then, from the moment I entered Ares Guild, I had fought while holding back enough to avoid killing most of my opponents.

[P116]
Facing an attack like that head-on in my current condition would not have ended well.

[P117]
“Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung.”

[P118]
Go Jun hummed my name like a tune, then grinned.

[P119]
“You should see your face. You’re no hero. You’re just a rat. You’ll die crying and begging for your life.”

[P120]
I watched him approach, his voice almost cheerful. Then a thought struck me.

[P121]
“Did you take something?”

[P122]
“What?”

[P123]
“No, wait. In this case, should I say a Magic Gem instead of drugs?”

[P124]
“…!”

[P125]
The smile on Go Jun’s lips faded.

[P126]
I no longer needed an answer. His face had given me one.

[P127]
“Hah.”

[P128]
I let out a hollow laugh.

[P129]
The rage that had briefly paralyzed my mind and body ebbed, and I could finally see the situation clearly.

[P130]
“Of course. That’s how you did it.”

[P131]
“Seeing someone in a new light” and “improving by leaps and bounds” were just four-character idioms. At least when it came to martial arts.

[P132]
Martial strength had to be honed through training and real combat.

[P133]
Even with the System, I could not have grown stronger at that rate. Go Jun certainly could not have done it.

[P134]
No one became this strong in only two months.

[P135]
There had only ever been one answer.

[P136]
“You took one. You really did, you fucking idiot.”

[P137]
I couldn’t hold back my laughter.

[P138]
It wasn’t amusement. It was disgust. Go Jun had chosen to give up being human and become a monster, and the sheer stupidity of it kept making me laugh.

[P139]
“Fuck, I’ve never seen an idiot like you. You couldn’t beat me any normal way, so you started sucking down Magic Gems? If you were going to do that, why not go to Magic Johnson? I bet that guy would’ve taken real good care of you with his magic wand.”

[P140]
I had hit a nerve. Go Jun’s face went rigid, and his already-red eyes darkened further.

[P141]
“Shut your fucking—”

[P142]
“Just shut up and listen, you son of a bitch.”

[P143]
*Thud. Thud.*

[P144]
Rubble and chunks of marble fell away as I got up.

[P145]
I cracked my stiff neck from side to side and stared at him.

[P146]
“What? You set off a few Monster Waves with an S-grade Magic Gem and pissed yourself over how well it worked? Watched people die because you barely lifted a finger and thought you were a god? No, sir, you fucking moron. You’re just a monster. At best, you’re some idiot side character with a Named Monster for a constellation.”

[P147]
“Shut up!”

[P148]
“Fuck off. Want me to give it a title, too? *Go Jun Swallows an S-Grade Magic Gem.*”

[P149]
“Jin Taekyuuung—!”

[P150]
*Fwoooooosh!*

[P151]
A gale rose with a tremendous wave of energy and swept through the area.

[P152]
I watched his power swell as if it were about to burst and answered calmly.

[P153]
“What, you fucking idiot?”

[P154]
I had never been afraid. Now that I knew what he had become, I had no reason to hesitate.

[P155]
He was a monster who had crossed the line, and he had to die by my hand today.

[P156]
For the old butler who had fallen into a darkness from which he would never return. For the people and Hunters who had died in the Monster Waves.

[P157]
And… for me, furious at this goddamned reality.

[P158]
“You have to die.”

[P159]
I bit out the words with all my heart. Go Jun’s blood-red figure blurred.

[P160]
*Whoooooosh! KABOOM!*

[P161]
The red Aura Blade stopped above my head.

[P162]
The tremendous pressure coming through White Flame’s spear blade made my wrists throb, and my ankles sank deep into the ground.

[P163]
But I did not give way. At least the power I wielded had been built through countless hours of training and insight, with the good fortune of the System added on top.

[P164]
“Get lost, you drugged-up bastard.”

[P165]
*Rrrrmmble!*

[P166]
I grinned into Go Jun’s wide eyes and drove my fist forward with all my strength.

[P167]
*Wham!*

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
